rationale: The randomized Parkinson comparison counted falls with strawberry extract in both formulations. The seven-fruit admissions estimate was near null and the six-fruit sway crossover was inconclusive. The 2015 strawberry-powder rats fell sooner than blueberry-fed rats from a stationary rod and later from a wide plank. Strawberry and control did not differ clearly across the three timed tests. The older extract studies and 2006 irradiated-rat learning study add distinct preparations and outcomes. A purified procyanidin B2 comparison counted fewer provoked falls under experimental demyelination at the higher dose, with no strawberry arm and a figure-to-prose latency conflict. The single-group Rett extension adds two people with a fall during a cannabidiol formulation study, with no fruit assignment or recurrence count. These sources give no transferable direction for raw strawberries and recurrent Parkinson falls. Twelve original records and related full-body paths remain open.

The recovered original dietary trial tested different formulated fat mixtures and measured plasma lipids, with two transient gastrointestinal complaints during the macadamia-rich period. Other human comparisons measured cognition, digestion or fatigue. Whole-kernel canine toxicity and rat brain tissue findings supply no transferable effect direction for dietary cold-pressed oil and Parkinson resting tremor.

The recovered 1949 Parkinsonian series reports smaller tremor amplitude under drug treatment with unchanged incidence and frequency. Peanut oil was only an injected drug carrier, with no oil-only comparison. The separate oral oil studies address allergy, activity, metabolism or other outcomes. No signed result transfers to cold-pressed peanut oil and Parkinson resting tremor.

The Parkinson dietary study includes cantaloupe in a shared menu. The original supplement and main paper report total motor scores with no separate resting tremor or fruit contrast. The case-control reply pools cucurbits and concerns diagnosis. Seed and peel motor proxies and traditional source tables supply no transfer to raw flesh or resting tremor.

Juice and cabergoline comparisons measure drug concentrations. Cabergoline improved a resting-tremor outcome in another pilot, and an antibiotic interaction reported improvement in resting tremor or rigidity in some patients. Fresh pulp and segments changed the exposure to different medicines. These comparisons leave both the raw-fruit transfer and the symptom response untested. The shared diet, induced animal signs and public accounts supply no eligible direction.

Ground soybeans were compared during standard levodopa treatment, with no separate resting-tremor estimate in the available abstract. Oil-vehicle and placebo comparisons address essential postural or voice tremor and do not isolate a refined-oil effect. No signed comparison transfers to this claim.

High-dose fennel oil toxicity reports describe tremor in rats with uncertain cohort overlap. Isolated fenchone had no tremors in a healthy-rat toxicity comparison. The Parkinson models measure imposed posture or coordination, and crushed-seed feeding measures general activity. Roasting changes fruit volatiles. No source supplies a transferable resting-tremor direction for eating toasted fennel seed.

The separate mouse rest-tremor comparison gives a minimal easing signal. Fresh celery stalk contains two measured extract flavones, while dietary equivalence, active mediator and transfer to human Parkinson disease remain uncertain. Clinical drug and conversational reports give no eligible separate outcome.

The pooled turkey-frequency tile lacks preparation, a pairwise estimate and a rest-tremor item. A firsthand turkey account reports reduced perceived medication effect without describing tremor. Controlled protein and meal comparisons report general tremor, motor symptoms, blood pressure or OFF time. Neither signed direction transfers to baked turkey and separately measured resting tremor.

The oral fig-and-almond syrup arm recorded 3 of 40 tremor events versus 0 of 40 in each comparison arm. The Iranian register identifies a differently composed almond-and-raisin comparator, and both sources concern children with ADHD receiving methylphenidate. Sparse counts, an unspecified tremor phenotype and no raw-fruit comparison block an eligible sign for Parkinson resting tremor. The Parkinson diet shares figs across groups; the remaining fruit, bark and flower-bud studies do not measure the frozen outcome.

The near-neutral pooled-tremor tile lacks oil grade and a separate rest item, an interpretable pairwise estimate or uncertainty. Two copies count as one cohort. The injected exact-grade mouse exposure measured motor proxies, and the whole-diet adverse events cannot isolate the oil or rest symptoms.

Mixed broccoli and white mustard tea has one favorable report and unspecified transient worsening, without an isolated or subtype-specific comparison. Human biomarker and animal studies use other forms or outcomes. The plant preparation evidence and the modern traditional interpretation leave the effect of toasted seed open.

A Parkinson placebo comparison separates rest tremor and reports a small favorable isolated caffeine estimate with intervals spanning zero. Chromatography verifies the link to brewed black tea, with different amounts and food matrix. Open-label mixed responses and reported worsening with coffee limit transfer. The brewed-tea effect remains uncertain.

The refined-oil DICe pilot favored sunflower over coconut for exploratory switching. MEMO and the Jenkins trial did not distinguish high-oleic sunflower from active comparators for executive change. Seed oil improved recognition memory in scopolamine-treated mice and students improved recall in a single-group study. Very high-fat sunflower and palm-kernel diets worsened radial-maze performance. A second rat study found more working-memory errors after a combined sunflower and saline regimen than in untreated controls. The handling difference limits oil attribution. The Parkinson clinical record measured a composite and the Parkinson models used a shared injected vehicle. No interpretable direction transfers to cold-pressed sunflower oil and a separate Parkinson executive outcome.

The ALS safflower arm worsened on a composite that contains swallowing. The two singer safflower arms moved in opposite directions on reflux totals, with no separate swallowing item in any report. TRIHEP3 lists a distinct safflower cohort from the drug and training dysphagia trials. The ataxia swallowing estimate used an MCT comparator. The safflower oleogel panel spat out the samples, and the cold-pressed mouse diet measured immunity. No directional estimate transfers to cold-pressed safflower oil and Parkinson dysphagia. Item-level ALS and reflux results plus lead-specific body access remain open.

The crude ENRGISE serious fall comparison and the pooled Alzheimer corn-or-soy comparison point to slightly more participants with falls in the comparator groups. Event counts are sparse or imprecise, neither study identifies recurrent Parkinson falls and the pooled study does not isolate corn oil. Timed mobility studies and chemically injured animals measure different outcomes. The COPD and NUTRIMAL trials add mixtures rather than refined corn oil attribution. No observed direction transfers to the frozen comparison. Original full-text and direct fall-count searches remain open.

The quantified Religa survey associates olive-oil quantity with lower HADS anxiety outside Parkinson disease (adjusted −1.86 points, 95% CI −3.54 to −0.18). Oil grade was unknown and the unadjusted item did not survive multiplicity correction. The small Parkinson heatmap supplies contextual evidence. A verified cold-pressed oil comparison shows favorable exploratory behavior on selected tests in young rats, with other maze results inconclusive and no clinical outcome. DieTBra uses exact cold-pressed oil outside Parkinson, but all active arms improved and the critique reports lower post-treatment anxiety in diet alone. MEDI-PD's whole-diet comparison is inconclusive. The observed human ingredient–symptom association supports a minimal easing lean. Direct matched clinical and DieTBra arm results remain open.

Fourteen diagnosed Parkinson participants completed three months of brewed green tea. Their mean Fatigue Severity Scale score rose from 28.4 to 32.1, and the same cohort's dissertation gives median scores of 27 and 30.5. This is one uncontrolled observation with no paired variance or exact fatigue p value. A postoperative brewed-tea trial favored less fatigue in a different clinical setting. Parkinson observational sources use ungraded tea, pooled domains or total caffeine and provide no comparable separate brewed-tea change. The exact exposure and outcome support a tentative worsening link. No controlled Parkinson fatigue estimate or recovered full body for the Jiang fly paper was verified.

The Isfahan trial randomized 92 adults with Parkinson disease and directly compared orally consumed ground dried Sargol stigma powder with placebo. The adjusted DASS depression difference was −4.58 points (95% CI −8.34 to −0.81), favoring less depression. The ground powder was delivered in a fixed-dose tablet. Depression was a secondary endpoint and the trial was powered for a biomarker. An independent Tehran trial favors saffron on Hamilton depression scores, with two other depression measures inconclusive and capsule processing unverified. The Shiraz non-Parkinson stigma adjunct comparison is inconclusive and the isolated crocin mouse result is indirect. The matched Parkinson comparison supports easing and therefore opposes the frozen worsening claim. Effects at ordinary meal quantities and independent replication with the same preparation remain open.

The Isfahan trial directly assessed Parkinson fatigue after swallowing tablets containing dried Sargol stigma powder versus placebo. The adjusted difference was −9.20 points (95% CI −13.76 to −4.65), favoring less fatigue. The primary sample-size calculation was for a biomarker. The original public registration omitted the standalone fatigue scale and the first archived revision listing it postdates receipt of the outcome manuscript. The fixed preparation and single eligible Parkinson trial keep the direction provisional. Non-Parkinson extract comparisons are mixed or inconclusive. The Ashtiani syrup lacks a control and its initial fatigue mean exceeds the scale range described in its own methods. The matched Parkinson sample supports easing and opposes the frozen worsening claim. Earlier protocol materials and independent Parkinson fatigue comparisons remain open.

Whole dried dates in healthy adults gave very similar reported abdominal pain values and no clear difference. The whole-date mouse study did not resolve a change versus control. Extract animal studies report evoked responses with sedation, motor suppression or conflicting trial details. Published Parkinson studies or protocols cover combined nutritional or herbal exposures and supply no transferable ingredient-specific pain direction. The human diary uncertainty, protected outcome tables and registered pain-item reporting remain open.

The pooled non-fried fish heatmap gives a small inverse graphical association with self-rated Parkinson slowness. It lacks a salmon or grilling field and a pair-specific estimate. The German preschool and infant trials report inconclusive peg-test and Bayley psychomotor comparisons without a signed estimate for either endpoint. Mouse locomotion favored an isolated roe fraction, with remote preparation and outcome fit. The mixed-fish hip-fracture trial stopped early and gives no results. No interpretable direction transfers to grilled salmon and clinical Parkinson bradykinesia. Obtain the full child trial tables and continue the original-pair and preparation-specific searches.

The dried-leaf Parkinson pilot reports cognition and salivation without an apathy result. In healthy adults, the controlled dried-leaf comparison gave higher alertness before the stress task and lower task-associated alertness after the same dose. A probable mixed-sage trial family gives no clear mood contrast. Compound studies describe movement in animals, and a Parkinson effort task uses apathy as a participant characteristic. These outcomes do not establish a directional effect on clinical apathy from dried sage. The pilot's secondary timetable and the original constituent study tables remain open.

The controlled whole-blueberry powder crossover in 43 adults with functional gastrointestinal disorders gives a small favorable constipation score difference of -0.3 (95% CI -0.7 to 0.2), with uncertainty on both sides of zero. Eating powder made from whole berries provides a limited preparation bridge to raw blueberries. Constipation reports during powder supplementation, including resolution after a pause in one uncontrolled case, limit that transfer. The ACID safety comparison used purified bilberry and black currant rather than blueberries. Parkinson food cohorts and the registered blueberry motor trial do not give a blueberry-specific constipation severity contrast. The sign supports only a minimal easing lean.

A clinical case describes immediate drooling during a likely allergic reaction after fresh fig in one child, with corroborating fig sensitization but no oral challenge. The randomized drug-plus-syrup study reports drooling in 17, 15 and 5 of 40 children across the fig-and-almond, almond-and-raisin and placebo arms. Those event counts, acute swelling and different formulations provide adverse-reaction context. They do not estimate a change in Parkinson drooling severity. The clinical parkinsonism sources do not test raw fig.

A paper-filtered coffee crossover reported less acute mental fatigue than flavored water in healthy habitual caffeine consumers. The measured caffeine component links this exposure to a Parkinson placebo-controlled capsule trial, whose Fatigue Severity Scale point estimates favor easing with intervals spanning both directions. The small regular-versus-decaf espresso comparison has mixed individual responses and shares brewed coffee across arms. Turkish coffee gave an inconclusive fatigue comparison with later raw means favoring water. Taken together, the two separately interpretable signs support only a minimal easing lean against the frozen worsening hypothesis.

Two separate placebo comparisons of oral standardized stigma extract in adults without Parkinson disease favor a specifically measured insomnia outcome, one on the Insomnia Severity Index and one on pooled Athens Insomnia Scale. Oral stigma preparations share the botanical source and documented constituents. The Parkinson Sargol powder trial favors overall sleep quality but does not isolate insomnia severity. The older-adult ISI pilot is inconclusive, the perimenopause preprint has an inconclusive global sleep result, and another Affron trial has inconclusive sleep disturbance. Different preparations, populations and sleep endpoints limit inference to a minimal easing signal. The application to Parkinson insomnia and the newer extraction and registration trails remain open.

Two independent small IBS trials measured a separate constipation severity domain and favored oral ginger capsules over placebo. Al-Jassim Table 1 and Rostamkhani Table 4 address the same patient-reported symptom and use the same ginger rhizome as a food, with different processing, dosing and diagnoses. Separate tablet and extract trials in multiple sclerosis, hypothyroidism, dyspepsia and occasional constipation provide related comparisons. The IBS pilot did not show a clear composite benefit and one constipation adverse event was reported with extract in migraine. Public accounts describe varied responses and simultaneous exposure changes. The registered Parkinson comparisons supply no reported constipation treatment estimate. Taken together the non-Parkinson symptom comparisons support only a minimal easing lean for the frozen question.

A double-blind randomized trial in 140 analyzed adults with functional constipation found lower four-week Rome III severity (-4.22, p < 0.001) and better Bristol stool form (+1.14, p < 0.001) with two tablespoons daily of raw extra-virgin versus refined olive oil, while excluding neurological disease, lacking an oil-free arm and omitting polyphenol assay. An ulcerative-colitis crossover abstract reports reduced GSRS constipation after extra-virgin olive oil, with full between-oil tables paywalled. In Parkinson disease, MEDI-PD's Mediterranean diet comparison was inconclusive (p = 0.600), the eight-person pilot was uncontrolled and multicomponent, and the KIM crossover encouraged olive oil in both phases; an epilepsy ketogenic cohort recorded 26.2% constipation without an oil-free control. The matched exposure and symptom contrast outside Parkinson disease supports only a minimal easing lean.

Three independent randomized human trials outside Parkinson disease report lower visual-analogue pain with encapsulated oral cinnamon bark powder versus starch placebo in primary dysmenorrhea (n=114, 24-72 h), migraine (n=43 completers, p<.001), and rheumatoid arthritis (n=36, abstract p<.001), alongside a high-attrition multiple-sclerosis trial with baseline imbalance and endpoint switch (VAS vs registered PQAS). Competing controlled trials show null upper abdominal pain for cinnamon-sesame macerate versus sesame oil and inconsistent exercise-soreness findings, while the single Parkinson rehabilitation case combined cassia with multimodal therapy. Differences in culinary ground exposure, non-Parkinson pain etiologies, and reporting limits keep the favorable easing signal at minimal_signal.

Two open-label randomized trials outside Parkinson disease report lower state anxiety after solid dark chocolate versus no snack before thyroid biopsy (n=99, STAI group-by-time p=.01) or mineral water in trainee nurses (n=47, 3 days), leaving expectancy effects unresolved. Competing randomized evidence includes a null acute state-anxiety trial in healthy adults (n=90), a small masked chronic-fatigue crossover without a direct between-treatment contrast (n=10), a brewed-cocoa crossover null versus water, and MEDI-PD restricting dark chocolate within whole-diet Parkinson counseling (HAM-A p=.745). No controlled evidence shows anxiety worsening; the non-Parkinson easing trials retain a minimal_signal against worsening.

Multiple randomized human trials outside Parkinson disease report lower pain after oral ginger rhizome powder or standardized extract versus placebo, including 11-day raw and heat-treated ground ginger capsules for eccentric muscle pain (n=74 across two studies), menstrual pain powder capsules (n=120), acute migraine add-on extract with ketoprofen (n=60, p=.03), and steamed GGE03 extract in functional dyspepsia (p<.001) and knee osteoarthritis. Substantive competing randomized trials show null pain effects for powdered ginger in knee osteoarthritis, migraine prevention, post-hysterectomy recovery, exercise joint pain (p=.690), acute post-exercise crossover, and craniotomy care. No controlled Parkinson pain trial exists (recruiting Ginger-PD NCT07882108 measures ghrelin/gut markers); preparation, population, and null-trial heterogeneity keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

An unblinded primary-dysmenorrhea trial reports larger VAS pain reduction when whole turmeric powder is added to naproxen (7.0 vs 5.6, p<.001), with an unresolved design and sample discrepancy versus its registry (149 parallel vs 90 crossover) and an implausible spread value, while an independent double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 42 completers with coronary slow flow phenomenon (PMID39085864, PMC11290174) reports improved secondary SF-36 Bodily Pain with 80 mg/day formulated nano-curcumin versus placebo (+13.9 vs -2.4, between-group and ANCOVA p<.001). Conversely, a double-blind hand-osteoarthritis pilot of whole turmeric powder (n=27) was inconclusive on primary one-month and between-group comparisons at all visits despite favorable three-month within-arm changes, and other formulated-extract or black-pepper-addition trials gave null primary between-arm pain contrasts. Non-Parkinson cohorts, formulated nano-curcumin versus culinary ground turmeric, attrition, registry conflicts, and null whole-powder pilot data keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

Two independent placebo-controlled menopause trials report less joint and muscular discomfort with oral Salvia officinalis fresh-tip extract (n=48 per-protocol of 80, p<.05) and dry extract (n=59, p<.001 with reversed table statistics), supported by a dose-comparison sage leaf throat-spray trial (n=164, p=.0021) and preclinical antinociception. Competing safety signals include one excessive-intake abdominal pain case (6/10) and a non-significant adverse-event count in an Alzheimer dry-extract trial (2 vs 0, p=.23), while perioperative/cancer rinse and mixed-herb trials give no isolated oral pain effect. Because no study evaluates fresh culinary sage or Parkinson pain severity, the controlled non-Parkinson discomfort reductions sustain only a minimal_signal against worsening.

Four non-Parkinson randomized oral lemon-balm trials report lower depressive symptoms versus placebo using powdered leaf capsules in stable angina (PMID29908682), leaf extract in type 2 diabetes (PMID37131158, n=44 completers, p=.001), phospholipid extract in emotional distress (PMID37927585), and postpartum capsules (p=.004, unresolved attrition). Competing controlled trials show null depression differences for dried-leaf lemon balm added to egg isolate (PMID21631360), baseline-imbalanced aqueous extract (PMID25680840), and inconclusive between-arm brewed tea in burn injury (DOI10.5812/traumamon.33630), while brewed-tea registrations await results and direct Parkinson depression trials remain absent. Preparation, population, and null-trial limits keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

One dried rosemary ground-leaf capsule trial added to SSRIs outside Parkinson disease reports a favorable BDI-II group-by-time contrast (PMID36343423, n=51 completers, p=.005) despite baseline imbalance without covariate adjustment, alongside a student capsule abstract reporting lower depression whose poster-extracted endpoint CI crosses zero (PMID29389474, SMD -0.30). Competing controlled trials show null depression contrasts for rosemary extract in methadone maintenance (Heidarzadeh 2026), healthy working men (UMIN000036762, p=.058), and a botanical blend (PMID38887495, p=.149), while fresh-derived rosemary-water trials omit clinical depression and a 2026 review pools heterogeneous end scores at SMD -0.29 (95% CI -1.01 to 0.42). No evidence indicates worsening; the dried-leaf SSRI trial retains a minimal_signal against worsening.

One randomized non-Parkinson depression trial reports lower DASS-21 scores when nigella oil extract is added to sertraline versus sertraline alone (PMID35548175, 18.6 vs 23.4, p<.001, with a one-point arithmetic discrepancy in printed change). A ground-seed premenstrual trial favored a composite mood domain rather than depression severity (PMID41267796), while crushed-seed Bond-Lader mood (PMID24412554) and mixed-product depression trials in hypothyroidism (p=.79) and multiple sclerosis were inconclusive, and a hemodialysis trial has unreported HADS results. Oil preparation, co-treatment, reporting discrepancy, and absence of toasted-seed or Parkinson trials keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

Two placebo-controlled oral Salvia officinalis extract trials in menopause (Zeidabadi 2020 dry extract, n=59, PSQI 9.4 to 5.6; Dimpfel 2021 fresh-tip extract, n=78) and a dormitory student tea trial versus brown sugar (Rigi 2024, n=128, room-allocated with unequal sugar and baseline typo) report better global sleep scores. An active-controlled primary-insomnia pilot comparing dried sage tea against chamomile was inconclusive (n=30, ISI p=.78/.83, baseline below eligibility) and the Newcastle Parkinson dried-sage pilot reported cognition and salivation without a sleep estimate. No controlled evidence shows insomnia worsening; the non-Parkinson sleep trials sustain a minimal_signal against worsening.

Two separately registered, placebo-controlled trials from the same research site report improved subjective PSQI (PMID37139438, 45 and 90 days) and objective actigraphy sleep efficiency, latency, and duration (PMID38288065, 7 days) using a proprietary nigella oil extract (BCO-5) in non-restorative sleepers. Competing trials show a null postmenopausal PSQI contrast with numeric discrepancies (PMID33603811, p=.45), superior latency/duration for melatonin over oil in an active crossover (PMID42819242), and a null multi-herb insomnia formula (p=.27). No controlled evidence shows insomnia worsening; proprietary oil extract transfer and absence of ground-seed or Parkinson trials keep the lean against worsening at minimal_signal.

One randomized non-Parkinson menopause trial reports lower one-month insomnia scores with sweet-basil (Ocimum basilicum) leaf extract versus placebo (IRCT20200104046001N1, n=60, 5.6 vs 11.0, p<.001). An independent triple-blind postpartum trial of dried sweet-basil leaf powder versus placebo found no clear total sleep-quality difference (IRCT20220926056046N2, 17.63 vs 16.15, adjusted p=.400), and injected isolated myrcene assays in mice measured barbiturate-induced sleep with opposite acute versus repeated timing effects. Absence of fresh culinary basil and Parkinson insomnia trials plus the null postpartum trial keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

One randomized tart-cherry concentrate trial outside Parkinson disease reports lower session mental fatigue by 9.5 points versus placebo (NCT04021342, 95% CI 2.5 to 16.5, p=.009; treatment-by-repetition p=.257). Multiple competing randomized trials report null fatigue differences for tart-cherry products in ulcerative colitis (n=35), acute task fatigue (n=27, p=.690), mixed cherry-apple juice (n=15), rugby players (n=11), marathon runners (n=35), sprinters (n=40), and pretraining athletes. No controlled trial tests whole dried cherries or Parkinson fatigue; the concentrate mental-fatigue result retains a minimal_signal against worsening.

One randomized non-Parkinson trial reports higher stool frequency (p=.0281) and softer stools (p=.04) with added orange pomace versus control, alongside increased gas/bloating and an unavailable separate constipation severity score (NCT02979496). Competing evidence includes a null pomace crossover for primary stool-frequency interaction (PMID36102329, p=.46), sequential null pasteurized orange juice (PMID30638420), an unadjusted older-adult survey (p=.054), uncontrolled multi-component Chagas and trifoliate-orange studies, and a Fox Insight pooled-fruit binary bowel category pointing opposite. No trial tests raw whole orange in Parkinson constipation; the pomace stool-frequency trial retains a minimal_signal against worsening.

No controlled or confounding-adjusted study estimates how eating poached eggs affects fall frequency in Parkinson disease or outside it. The Parkinson baseline figure (MVP-2024) plots only an unquantified near-zero inverse tile for unspecified egg frequency without coefficient, uncertainty interval, or poaching identity. An older-adult case-control study (PMID36915191) reports 2.03 versus 2.21 weekly egg portions in fall-with-fracture cases versus controls (unadjusted p=.07) with no preparation-specific or adjusted fall-frequency estimate. Nutri-Park compared protein timing rather than eggs, and remaining dietary or metabolic records omit fall counts; the claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

One placebo-controlled trial reports lower Hamilton anxiety scores with grape fruit extract in healthy older adults with low baseline anxiety (PMID29163162). Competing evidence includes an inconclusive 12-week whole-grape powder trial in postmenopausal women (PMC7257957, n=32 completers, numeric contrast omitted), mixed rotenone-rat behavioral proxies with dried Corinthian currants (open-field thigmotaxis p=.006 vs elevated-plus-maze p=.929), a null A53T mouse concentrate test, an order-affected acute juice study, and a pending college-student Hamilton trial (NCT07214428). No clinical trial tests raw grapes or Parkinson anxiety; the older-adult extract trial sustains a minimal_signal against worsening.

One exploratory randomized trial in healthy adults reports favorable POMS 2 tension-anxiety change with boiled waxy barley versus rice, though final group medians were equal at 43, foods were visibly different, and eight participants were excluded (PMID39064742). Competing trials show a null cooked barley-flour versus rice-flour crossover (n=23), inconclusive DASS anxiety with multi-component talbinah, no anxiety scale when both arms ate barley (PMID40336123), and whole-diet NutriAct excluding gait-affecting Parkinson disease. Matching boiled preparation in the exploratory healthy-adult trial sustains only a minimal_signal against worsening.

One randomized trial in forensic inpatients reports lower state anxiety over time with Atlantic salmon versus meat control (PMID25431880, p=.043; trait anxiety inconclusive; grilling and boiling pooled). Competing trials show null anxiety after angina fish advice with optional fish oil (+0.82, 95% CI -0.57 to 2.22) and null SDQ emotional symptoms in FINS-TEENS mixed oily-fish lunches (high-baseline subgroup favored meat), while Parkinson cohorts (MVP-2024, Fox Insight, Lithuanian MedDiet) pool fish or whole diets without species or poaching estimates. The non-Parkinson salmon trial sustains a minimal_signal easing lean.

One four-arm randomized adolescent conference abstract reports lower anxiety in the banana-only arm (regression -7.84, p<.001; preparation and full methods unavailable), alongside a nonrandom inpatient Ambon-banana comparison with baseline imbalance and a postoperative trial with conflicting reported t statistics (PMID40331125). Competing evidence includes a small null randomized healthy-adult Cavendish banana trial (n=20), uncontrolled Parkinson individualized nutrition with banana-flavored liquid, and separate levodopa-interaction observations without anxiety scores. No controlled Parkinson raw-banana anxiety trial exists; the adolescent randomized abstract sustains only a minimal_signal against worsening.

No controlled or confounding-adjusted study isolates virgin coconut oil for fatigue severity in or outside Parkinson disease. The Parkinson baseline figure (MVP-2024) plots only an unquantified tile without coefficient, grade, or uncertainty. Whole-diet ketogenic trials (Phillips 2018, military crossover, Choi 2024, KIM MCT diet where 9/37 improved and 9/37 worsened) do not isolate virgin coconut oil, and an unblinded chemotherapy study (PMID25163649) showed baseline imbalance (49.34 vs 36.38) with non-significant individual timepoint contrasts. Cyclist (FNRI-2007), runner (p=.99), and infection trials were null or omitted fatigue. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

No controlled study isolates refined coconut oil for postural instability in Parkinson disease or outside it. The Parkinson baseline figure (MVP-2024) plots only an unquantified tile without numeric coefficient, confidence interval, or oil grade, while PRO-PD observational analyses report only composite total scores. The multiple-sclerosis balance report (PMID36594273) bundled extra-virgin oil with EGCG, had baseline imbalance (49 vs 43), and reported within-arm tests only, while the Parkinson MCT ketogenic study (PMID38561682) showed no clear mobility difference. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

No controlled study isolates virgin coconut oil for daytime sleepiness severity. The Parkinson baseline figure (MVP-2024) gives only an unquantified inverse tile without oil grade, adjustment, or uncertainty. The Parkinson ketogenic diet trial (PMID30098269) varied entire meal plans rather than isolating virgin coconut oil, pooled caregiver narratives (10.18103/mra.v12i4.5316) lack standardized scores and stratification, and ISRCTN13221188 provides no Epworth or virgin-oil estimate. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

No controlled study isolates virgin coconut oil for apathy severity. The Parkinson baseline figure (MVP-2024) plots only an unquantified tile for motivation/initiative without oil grade, adjustment, or error limits. The Parkinson ketogenic MCT feeding study (PMID38561682) found no clear between-group diary apathy difference without isolating virgin coconut oil, and KIM (NCT05469997) reported no post-diet apathy comparison. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

No controlled human study isolates cold-pressed olive oil for bradykinesia severity. The Parkinson baseline graphic (MVP-2024) plots only an unquantified self-rated slowness tile rather than examiner-rated bradykinesia, and observational or whole-diet Mediterranean studies (PMID29081890, PMID32319358, PMID21535916) evaluate total scores or dietary patterns without isolating olive oil grade or bradykinesia. Buriram (TCTR20210303005) tested cannabinoids in a shared olive-oil vehicle with inconclusive UPDRS III, and MPTP mouse oral olive-oil motor comparisons (PMC10526674) were unclear while injected EVOO is non-oral and non-bradykinesia. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

No controlled or statistically clear evidence links cold-pressed flaxseed oil to bradykinesia severity. In early Parkinson disease (PMID34127758), plasma alpha-linolenic acid was non-significantly correlated with examiner-rated body bradykinesia (age-adjusted p=.171, sex-adjusted p=.372) and did not track dietary intake. Flaxseed omega-3 plus vitamin E trials (PMID28342967, PMID30554092) combined vitamin E, lacked isolated bradykinesia items, and reported inconclusive UPDRS Part III, while older-adult FAB motor series (p=.140) and rat activity (p=.595) were null and isolated-ALA animal tasks do not transfer. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

No controlled clinical comparison establishes an anxiety effect for cold-pressed flaxseed oil. The only human flaxseed-oil anxiety trial (DOI10.23937/2474-3631/1510010) found an inconclusive final Beck anxiety contrast (p=.31) with low baseline scores and unverified pressing. Parkinson omega-3 plus vitamin-E trials report no isolated anxiety item or oil-only arm, and rodent elevated-plus-maze proxies (rotenone, maternal separation with null light-dark and higher amygdala inflammation, haloperidol oil-alone null) do not supply an eligible clinical sign. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

No controlled comparison against an inactive control isolates cold-pressed flaxseed oil for constipation severity. The registered hemodialysis trial (NCT02103556, PMID25238699) compared flaxseed, olive, and active laxative mineral oil (n=50) and found an inconclusive between-oil interaction (p=.15) with unverified pressing grade; a lipid trial (sjams.2018.v06i01.047) logged 2/57 vs 5/55 constipation adverse events against liquid paraffin without severity scoring; plasma ALA was unrelated to Wexner constipation (PMID34127758); and petroleum-ether extracted oil gave a nonmonotonic rodent wet-stool response. Consistent with claim 0072, the claim moves from legacy 51 to open.

One single-blind oral flaxseed-oil osteoarthritis trial (DOI10.36347/sjams.2019.v07i09.031) and a potentially overlapping rheumatoid-arthritis report from the same investigators (Vyas 2020, independence uncertain) report lower rest and movement arthritis pain, though pressing grade is unreported and dosing/numeric reporting is inconsistent. Competing trials show null pain contrasts for flaxseed versus corn oil after ACL surgery (p=.96), versus linoleic acid in rheumatoid arthritis (n=22), and versus vitamin E in cyclic mastalgia (p=.142), while Parkinson flaxseed-omega-3 plus vitamin-E trials omit pain items. The single-blind oral arthritis pain comparison retains only a minimal_signal easing lean.

One placebo-controlled menopause trial of fresh Salvia officinalis tip extract reports lower secondary POMS fatigue (PMID33615001, p=.029, without an arm-by-time fatigue table; separate sleep-exhaustion item unchanged). A dry-extract menopause trial gave an inconclusive exhaustion contrast (IRCT2015111713940N2, p=.634), Spanish-sage essential oil reduced acute healthy task fatigue (different species), Newcastle PD sage trial omitted fatigue, and a single multi-exposure FAERS report cannot attribute fatigue to sage. Extract transfer and multiplicity keep the lean against worsening at minimal_signal.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Parkinson trial of isolated caffeine capsules reports a 6-week UPDRS III bradykinesia subscore difference of -1.70 points (95% CI -3.10 to -0.31; limb-only CI crossed zero; PMID22855866), bridged to brewed black tea by infusion chromatography showing lower caffeine per cup (PMID40647065). Competing evidence includes an inconclusive longer-term caffeine total-motor trial (-0.48, 95% CI -3.21 to 2.25; PMID28954882), an observational PPMI preprint reporting faster progression (body unverified), non-replicated LRRK2 composite findings, and mixed rat exploratory activity. The direct Parkinson bradykinesia constituent RCT supports limited_clinical_link (51), matching claim 0904.

One randomized student trial of oral dried Thymus vulgaris leaves reports more participants in the normal HADS anxiety range at one month (40/53 vs 31/53 from 27/53 vs 30/53 baseline; PMID38039009), but carries major reporting and registry discrepancies (implausible baseline SD, overlapping cutoffs, contradictory within-control test, and 86 triple-blind registered vs 106 double-blind reported). An independent wild-thyme extract trial found null FDDQL anxiety (+3.21, p=.410; PMID42930530), and preclinical assays test isolated terpenes or extracts in rodents. The student oral-leaf comparison sustains only a minimal_signal easing lean.

Two randomized non-Parkinson trials of formulated turmeric extracts in knee symptoms report favorable walking speed (+0.08 vs +0.01 m/s, p<.05 with minor intergroup conflict; PMID29316908) and 80-meter walk time (-11.0 vs -6.8 s, Mann-Whitney p=.0011; PMID34045905). Competing trials show null 4-meter gait speed in healthy aging (p=.9; PMID29951592), null 40-meter walking with Curcugen (p=.604; PMID35010916), an older-adult pilot numerically favoring placebo (n=17, +.014 vs +.103 m/s), and null isolated curcumin open-field speed in rotenone rats. Formulated extracts and non-Parkinson knee cohorts keep the lean against worsening at minimal_signal.

One open-label randomized trial in acute COVID-19 reports fewer participants with day-4 fatigue after oral Nigella sativa seed oil versus control (12/30 vs 25/30, adjusted OR 0.15, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.48; PMID36425571). Competing randomized evidence includes closer ground-nigella-seed trials showing mixed/null day-10 fatigue (PMID36142070) and null physical PMS symptoms (PMID41267796), plus a null nigella-flax multiple-sclerosis fatigue trial (DOI10.34172/hpp.44662). Seed oil, open-label design, acute infection binary presence, and absence of Parkinson fatigue trials keep the lean against worsening at minimal_signal.

One controlled rodent experiment reports higher evoked mechanical and thermal pain thresholds with whole Juglans regia walnut oil in inflammatory and diabetic mice (n=7/group; mechanical fold below tramadol; DOI10.1016/j.bjp.2018.03.007), supported by independent composition analyses linking linoleic proportions across extraction methods (PMID30065427, PMID30651416) and a green-walnut injection assay. No controlled human clinical pain trial tests cold-pressed walnut oil (pain rose in an uncontrolled advanced-cancer mixed-oil ketogenic cohort, and ACTRN12622000083796 uses walnut oil in its placebo without results). Preclinical transfer keeps the easing lean at minimal_signal.

One randomized postpartum trial reports lower after-pain intensity and quality with 1.1 g oral sesame-oil capsules versus placebo (n=86; abstract only, roasting unverified, registry interval conflict; DOI10.1016/j.hermed.2024.100885), alongside an oral episiotomy-pain trial favoring sesame at later doses with an inconclusive overall group-by-time interaction (PMID41354976). Topical limb-trauma massage trials use a non-oral route, while dyspepsia and Parkinson cannabinoid studies used sesame oil in both arms or open-label without an oil comparator. Abstract-only reporting, unverified toasting, and postpartum pain limit the easing lean to minimal_signal.

One randomized weight-loss diet trial comparing refined sesame oil against refined sunflower oil reports lower anxiety in its abstract (p=.011; DOI10.1108/NFS-12-2022-0407), though exact contrast definitions and arm means remain unavailable, no oil-free control was included, and the oil was refined rather than cold-pressed. Injected sesame oil increased rat anxiety-like behavior (PMID24409407), inhaled aroma studies test a non-oral route, and a Parkinson cannabinoid trial gave sesame oil to both arms (PMID38487964). The human oral comparison retains only a minimal_signal against worsening.

No controlled human study estimates whether consuming ground nutmeg worsens constipation severity. A single medullary thyroid carcinoma case (PMC1673758) reduced secretory diarrhea from 6.7 to 2.6 stools/day after replacing prior drugs with high-dose ground nutmeg, which cannot estimate constipation from culinary intake. The 1976 nutmeg-constipation letter (PMID942762) lacks verified accessible full text, and animal studies measure dry stool output, experimental diarrhea (aqueous extract null), or charcoal transit proxies rather than clinical constipation. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

Two randomized human gastrointestinal trials outside Parkinson disease report lower pain with anise versus placebo: ground anise powder lowered week-4 epigastric pain in functional dyspepsia (0.38 vs 2.05 vs cornstarch; IRCT2013101214980) and enteric-coated anise oil eased abdominal pain in IBS (NCT02364830). An acute COVID-19 anise-and-rock-sugar sachet trial favored abdominal pain with an ambiguous table ratio label (RR 0.55), Ushaq capsule composition remains pending, and rodent assays provide preclinical context. Gastrointestinal non-Parkinson pain etiology keeps the lean against worsening at minimal_signal.

One randomized crossover in 24 adults with medication-related xerostomia reports easier subjective swallowing in 8/24 after a cold-pressed roasted-kernel sunflower oil mouth rinse (spat out) versus 2/24 after water (unadjusted p=.031; measured saliva flow favored water; PMID33314461). Parkinson surveys link dry mouth with swallowing complaints without assigning oil, a baseline PRO-PD poster found null total symptoms (+2, p=.787), and an infant aspiration case series documents lipoid pneumonia with repeated oral oil without causal swallowing-severity testing. Remote rinse-vs-refined exposure and non-Parkinson xerostomia keep the lean against worsening at minimal_signal.

No controlled human comparison establishes an attention effect for toasted cumin. The only clinical trial (PMID42088310) tested distilled cumin essential oil in older adults and found inconclusive group interactions on both simple and complex attention. Analytical studies confirm cuminaldehyde after dry roasting without measuring cognition, a UK Parkinson dietary survey found no corrected nonmotor cumin association, and EEG odor or rodent memory assays do not test clinical attention. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

One triple-blind randomized trial outside Parkinson disease reports earlier first postoperative defecation after oral Cuminum cyminum extract capsules versus placebo (PMID38965524). A randomized multi-herb digestive mixture favored constipation at week one (p=.049) but was inconclusive at week two (p=.152) with 10% mixture in control and cannot isolate cumin, while an IBS essential-oil study lacked a control and rat studies diverge across wet stool versus slowed charcoal transit. No trial isolates ground cumin in chronic Parkinson constipation; the postoperative oral-extract RCT sustains only a minimal_signal easing lean.

No controlled trial shows that eating poached trout affects depressive symptom severity. The only randomized trout feeding trial (JGG2017-SHAPOURI-113, n=96 older adults) found a null adjusted GDS-15 difference (-0.17, 95% CI -0.48 to 0.15, p=.295) without specifying poaching or Parkinson disease. Angina fatty-fish advice had an interval crossing zero, and marine omega-3 supplement evidence is contradictory across small unspecified-species Parkinson pilots and VITAL-DEP (PMID34932079, higher incident depression with null mean PHQ-8). The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

One randomized 36-person older-adult meal crossover reports fewer six-hour post-meal spatial working-memory errors and better strategy after whole freeze-dried red raspberry powder versus control (NCT03879213, p<.05). A black-raspberry Alzheimer pilot measured global CDR without executive subscales, four-berry and multicomponent capsule trials do not isolate raspberry, and rodent studies are split between high-fat-diet benefit and Alzheimer-model null results. Acute meal testing, powder vs intact frozen fruit, and non-Parkinson population keep the lean against worsening at minimal_signal.

Two randomized chemoradiotherapy trials report less severe dysphagia with formulated turmeric or curcumin versus placebo: bio-enhanced turmeric capsules lowered grade 3 dysphagia (25% and 20% vs 60% placebo; PMID34161952 abstract) and nanocurcumin prevented worsening on instrumental Penetration-Aspiration Scale scores in 64 completers (2.91 vs 3.72 from equal 2.91 baselines; ARSHIDA-REF2023-063210). An oral-fibrosis trial has sparse counts and discordant p values, and a Parkinson multi-supplement registry reports pill-swallowing complaints without isolated turmeric severity data. Radiation mucositis and formulated extracts differ substantially from neurologic Parkinson dysphagia and grated turmeric, keeping the lean at minimal_signal.

One randomized open-label dysmenorrhea trial (n=80) reports lower three-month menstrual weakness scores with fennel soft capsules versus no medication (6.65 to 2.88 vs 6.39 flat, p=.001; abstract prints a conflicting control value; PMID25085020). Two other dysmenorrhea trials were inconclusive for fatigue (essential oil overall p=.08 with differential discontinuation; 2007 extract p=.058 without reported direction), and crushed-seed infusion and honey-mixture surveys lack controlled fatigue data. Unblinded design, reporting conflict, null comparators, and non-Parkinson menstrual weakness keep the lean against worsening at minimal_signal.

One randomized weight-loss diet trial comparing refined sesame oil against refined sunflower oil concludes lower depression in its abstract (p=.013; DOI10.1108/NFS-12-2022-0407), though exact contrast definitions, arm estimates, an oil-free arm, and cold-pressed processing remain unavailable. A Parkinson cannabinoid trial gave sesame oil to both arms with inconclusive depression scores (PMID38487964), and rat forced-swim outcomes varied across endpoints. The human oral oil comparison sustains only a minimal_signal easing lean.

One randomized pediatric chemotherapy-mucositis trial (n=60) reports faster local pain reduction with topical summer-savory extract gel added to routine care versus placebo gel (IRCT2016061813691N7). The closer oral dried-leaf knee-osteoarthritis trial (n=39 analyzed of 60) found an inconclusive between-group pain contrast (p=.38; IRCT2013112515542N1), and rodent assays split between formalin/writhing attenuation and null 6-OHDA rat carvacrol hyperalgesia (PMID29489959). Topical mucositis route and the null oral knee trial keep the easing lean for fresh culinary summer savory at minimal_signal.

Two randomized gastrointestinal trials outside Parkinson disease report lower fatigue-adjacent ratings with anise versus placebo: ground anise powder favored week-12 SF-36 vitality in functional dyspepsia (IRCT2013101214980) and enteric-coated anise oil showed lower tiredness in IBS (3.15/2.74 vs 3.94/3.54, three-arm p<.001, though a later review disagrees; NCT02364830). A ground-anise menopause trial omitted separate fatigue severity and a honey-mixture survey gave no isolated estimate. Non-Parkinson GI cohorts and generic vitality/tiredness outcomes keep the lean against worsening at minimal_signal.

Three oral ground Cinnamomum verum experiments from one research program report improved rotarod, open-field movement, and shorter timed pole turning/descent in aged A53T (PMID32889602, n=5-6/group; 2025 correction replaced separate benzoate histology panels) and MPTP mouse Parkinson models (PMID24946862, PMID31119595). No human clinical gait-speed trial isolates ground cinnamon (Park 2026 OA15.04 reports intake behavior only). Same-program mouse agility proxies without clinical gait data sustain only a minimal_signal against worsening.

One randomized weight-loss diet trial comparing refined sesame oil against refined sunflower oil favors sesame on fatigue in its abstract (p=.002; DOI10.1108/NFS-12-2022-0407), though exact contrast definitions, arm means, an oil-free arm, and cold-pressed grade remain unavailable. An open-label Parkinson cannabidiol trial logged fatigue in 8/13 participants taking sesame-oil carrier without an oil comparator (PMID33381646). The human oral comparison sustains only a minimal_signal against worsening.

No controlled clinical comparison establishes that brewed lemongrass worsens daytime sleepiness severity. In the 1986 healthy-volunteer tea study (Leite 1986), morning sleepiness after two active brew conditions (16/50 and 17/50) versus placebo (13/50) gave an inconclusive paired comparison, while the 5/11 acute morning somnolence reports came from a separate uncontrolled group without a validated sleepiness severity scale. A four-case Parkinson essential-oil report (PMID41250562) tested inhaled/topical oil and found daytime sleep unchanged in all four cases. The claim therefore moves from legacy 51 to open.

One double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial in 66 outpatients with overactive bladder reports lower end-of-treatment Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (6.33 vs 9.73, p<.001), urgency-frequency item (2.82 vs 4.18, p<.001), and Urgency Severity Scale (2.67 to 1.64) after a topical cinnamon patch versus placebo patch, while daytime voiding frequency was inconclusive (p=.79; NCT03532789). Supporting oral rodent evidence shows Cinnamomum cassia powder lowered cyclophosphamide-cystitis void counts (PMC8716214), whereas a rat distension assay diverged between cystitis (reduced) and uninflamed controls (increased). Topical route, non-Parkinson OAB etiology, and animal divergence keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

No controlled study isolates roasted potato for daily OFF time in Parkinson disease. Low-protein redistribution crossovers (PMID16773618, PMID18019394, 3.5 vs 5 hours daily OFF, p=.01) varied formulated low-protein diets rather than roasted potato; Baroni menus allowed potatoes in both arms with inconclusive ordinal OFF distributions (p=.054); Dresden measured ON-state cold potato salad intake; and N-DOSE (NCT05589766) awaits posted results without a potato-specific OFF analysis.

No completed controlled clinical study tests ground ginger for Parkinson dyskinesia severity. Active or completed Parkinson ginger registrations (NCT07882108, IRCT20251028067794N1, NCT05001217) have no posted dyskinesia results. Preclinical signals diverge across preparations: a patent table (WO2024101890A1) reports lower AIM AUC for dried-rhizome extract with unverified route, n, and masking, whereas isolated zingerone (PMID21769642) did not suppress lesioned hindlimb stiffening and Duzhong Fang used a multi-herb blend.

No controlled clinical study isolates ground saffron for examiner-rated muscle rigidity severity in Parkinson disease. A randomized Tehran Parkinson trial of unspecified saffron capsules (n=52; DOI10.1016/j.hermed.2024.100968) found an inconclusive total MDS-UPDRS Part III contrast (p=.424) with no separate rigidity item; uncontrolled supplement charts and vegetarian menus do not isolate saffron; and injected safranal, crocin, or crocetinate rodent catalepsy assays are remote proxies.

No controlled study measures freezing of gait frequency after consuming ground turmeric. The Parkinson baseline figure (MVP-2024) plots only an unquantified pooled-spice tile; an older-adult curcumin pilot (NCT03085680) tracked walking speed without freezing counts; ZAZ2 tested multi-botanical granules on composite UPDRS; and rodent gait or beam-crossing studies (PMID35966793, PMID36742141) recorded no freezing episodes.

No controlled trial tests steamed brown rice on orthostatic lightheadedness severity in Parkinson disease. A randomized within-person study in 39 nursing-home residents (PMID26094950) reported less frequent seated postprandial hypotension after a half versus full rice serving without reporting rice grade, standing posture testing, or lightheadedness severity. Parkinson glucose and mixed-meal autonomic challenges document postprandial pressure drops without isolating steamed brown rice or standing symptom ratings.

No controlled clinical study tests consuming dried spearmint for Parkinson drooling severity. A Parkinson gum-chewing study (PMID20385891) increased swallow frequency without identifying flavor or measuring drooling severity; healthy-volunteer spearmint gum trials increased salivary secretion without clinical drooling outcomes; and a Sjogren multi-ingredient spray trial (NCT06313905) has no posted results or drooling endpoint.

No controlled study measures witnessed dream enactment or REM sleep without atonia after brewed lemongrass in Parkinson disease. A 50-volunteer brewed lemongrass tea study (Leite 1986) found no clear sleep or dream-recall differences, and a rat tea EEG study (PMID3762195) found no slow-wave or REM sleep changes. Inhaled or topical aroma reports, flavored-placebo nightmare counts, and mixed postpartum drinks do not test brewed tea or dream enactment.

No controlled human study shows that brewed green tea alters olfactory impairment severity in Parkinson disease. The PENSA double-blind EGCG trial (PMID40664536) found null 12-month olfaction change (+0.1, 95% CI -1.3 to 1.5, p=.853), the Kagoshima Parkinson cohort (PMID42816813) found null cross-sectional hyposmia by green-tea frequency (p=.854) and volume (p=.519), CHRIS (PMID42830263) excluded green tea, acute coffee/caffeine crossovers were null, and mouse concentrated-extract nasal histopathology (NTP-TR-585) did not test smell function.

No controlled study measures listener-rated speech intelligibility after cooked onion in Parkinson disease. A heated onion-peel extract trial (Cho 2024) reported adjusted self-rated URI hoarseness (p=.038) with baseline imbalance, null overall WURSS (p=.164), and no speech intelligibility metric; an allergy case (Albanesi 2019) recorded acute anaphylactic dysphonia; and Parkinson diet cohorts pool sofrito or omit cooked-onion speech contrasts.

No controlled study evaluates frozen blackberry on vocal loudness or low voice volume severity in Parkinson disease. Boysenberry-apple trials measure provoked throat irritation or a seven-item pediatric respiratory composite without acoustic loudness; Parkinson diet cohorts (MVP, Thai diet survey) pool berry species without voice-volume contrasts; and ethnobotanical jam or anaphylaxis reports supply no controlled loudness measurement.

No controlled study evaluates eating raw grapes on Parkinson hand dexterity, and non-Parkinson grape-product trials diverge in opposite directions across tasks. A grape-seed extract trial (NCT03526406) favored simple finger tapping (interaction p=.005) with complex tapping inconclusive, whereas a Concord grape juice crossover (PMID26864371) was slower on grooved pegboard in phase one (63.2 vs 60.4 s) and a mixed bilberry-grape juice trial (NCT00972972) was null on dominant-hand pegboard (p=.41).

No controlled study establishes a cold-pressed olive oil effect on shortened stride severity in Parkinson disease. A randomized fish-versus-olive-oil exergame trial (PMID30866834) found inconclusive single- and dual-task stride interactions (p=.753 and .537) with oil grade unspecified; NCT05485402 found no four-meter gait-speed difference; a stroke mouse model found no clear footprint benefit; and the PRIME whole-diet stride protocol (NCT07097103) awaits results.

No controlled study measures handwriting size after brewed green tea in Parkinson disease. The brewed green tea Parkinson pilot (DOI10.4236/jbbs.2015.56020) and LRRK2/Kagoshima cohorts report daily-living composites or nonmotor scales without isolated handwriting size; the six-month Parkinson caffeine capsule trial (PMID28954882) reported no MDS-UPDRS-II item differences; and a healthy caffeine crossover (PMID17010462) measured pen velocity/fluency rather than micrographia.

No controlled study isolates poached chicken for reduced facial expressiveness in Parkinson disease. Overlapping Parkinson cohort reports (PMID29081890, PMID40732955) analyze composite PRO-PD totals without a facial-expression item or poached preparation; Phillips 2018 (PMID30098269) included simmered chicken soup inside a whole ketogenic diet reporting total MDS-UPDRS III; and a corticobasal case history supplies no timed exposure contrast.

No controlled study tests consuming fresh chives for Parkinson dystonia severity. Parkinson diet menus (PMID32041265) list chives without species, individual dose, or separate dystonia scores; meal-protein dystonia reports (PMID1866021, PMID839864) omit chives; and onion, garlic, or Chinese-chive extracts and cellular assays do not evaluate fresh common chives or spontaneous Parkinson dystonia.

No controlled study measures visual hallucination frequency after consuming dried celery leaf in Parkinson disease. The celery-root mania case (PMID34370637) involved concurrent venlafaxine and St. John's wort without visual-frequency counts; a Parkinson butylphthalide trial (PMID30988766) reported only aggregate PDQ-39 scores with inconsistent adverse-event totals; and celery-seed safety (NCT06061926), Alzheimer composite (Gu 2024), and thyroid case reports omit visual hallucination frequency.

Prospective older-women citrus cohort (Sim et al. 2018, n=1,429) reported a null association for fall hospitalization (adjusted HR 1.01 per 20 g/day, 95% CI 0.99-1.04, p=0.345), while the Giovannini 2025/2026 Altemor pilot RCT (PMID:40694049, NCT06352099, n=36 elderly) tested a multi-ingredient diosmin+hesperidin+proanthocyanidins blend without isolating raw orange or enrolling Parkinson patients.

Two independent 12-week randomized placebo-controlled human trials in renal disease favored oral curcumin capsules for olfactory function over placebo (Nasution 2026 n=48 Sniffin Sticks composite TDI delta +3.56 p=0.010 and +4.00 p=0.002 vs +0.875; Malekmakan 2023 n=58 double-blind QOD p=0.045, self-assessment p=0.047, 20% vs 0% normosmia shift p=0.032), opposing the frozen worsening premise; non-Parkinson renal populations, formulated curcumin capsules instead of fresh grated turmeric, and capsule-standardization/Table 2 reporting limits keep the tier minimal.

Randomized formulated-curcumin trials outside Parkinson disease conflict across attention endpoints: Small 2018 (n=40) reported secondary Trail Making A improvement (p=0.04) and an exploratory 2026 eye-tracking test favored extract (p<0.05 across 35 outcomes), whereas Santos-Parker 2018 Flanker (p=0.97), Rainey-Smith 2016 battery (p=0.25), Kucukgoncu 2019 CPT (p=0.209), and Cox 2015 adjusted vigilance (p=0.168) were inconclusive; no Parkinson grated-turmeric attention trial exists.

Randomized sulforaphane and glucoraphanin capsule trials conflict on attention: Hei 2022 (n=172 schizophrenia) found inconclusive attention/vigilance change numerically favoring placebo (p=0.263) and Nouchi 2022 (n=144 older adults) found null Coding (p=0.83) and Stroop (p=1) despite Symbol Search p=0.03, while Ghannadi 2025 (n=63 pediatric ADHD methylphenidate adjunct, abstract-only) favored sulforaphane without confirming botanical source; no raw broccoli Parkinson attention evidence exists.

Two controlled freeze-dried strawberry studies reported no clear direct attention effect, and a four-berry smoothie trial reporting Attention Network changes did not isolate strawberry; fresh raw strawberry and clinical Parkinson attention remain unresolved.

Parkinson clinical trials of formulated curcuminoids (Ghodsi 2022 nanomicelle, Donadio phospholipid cohort) report composite motor scores without releasing a standalone passive muscle rigidity item, while rodent rotenone catalepsy models test isolated intragastric or injected curcumin; grated culinary turmeric and clinical rigidity remain unresolved.

Parkinson cohorts used cinnamon strictly as a diagnostic scratch-and-sniff odorant; an oral ground Cinnamomum cassia crossover in diabetes (Moreira 2024, n=19) found inconclusive breakfast-smell pleasantness (all p>=0.80) without a clinical olfactory scale, inhaled multi-odor smell training (Chao 2025, n=60) did not test ingestion or isolate cinnamon, and mixed essential-oil registration NCT07518394 posts no results; oral ground cinnamon effects on Parkinson olfaction remain open.

Parkinson studies involving olive oil either used it as a shared vehicle (Buriram TCTR20210303005 cannabis crossover), recorded baseline posture only, or reported composite diet scores (MVP cohort), while VIVI-OLIVE (NCT07829484) combines diet counseling with exercise outside Parkinson disease; isolated cold-pressed olive oil effects on Parkinson postural instability remain open.

Across 440 related assessments spanning Parkinson hallucination cohorts, fig-and-olive scopolamine rat memory studies, retail dried-fig contaminant surveillance, and dried-fig allergy reports, no study evaluates oral dried fig consumption against clinical visual hallucination frequency in Parkinson disease.

Across 40 related assessments, the whole dried Ajwa date crossover (NCT02288611, n=21) never published its mood diary, the Ajwa schizophrenia adjunct trial reported composite ratings only, and an acute date-drink alertness crossover (n=15) lacked verified fruit maturity and an apathy scale; dried date effects on Parkinson apathy remain open.

A personalized plant-rich Parkinson diet trial (PMID:41666212) reported apathy change without isolating raw banana, while a small open whole-banana trial outside Parkinson disease (DOI:10.12691/jfnr-10-12-2) reported inconclusive POMS2 vigor and fatigue subscales without an apathy instrument; raw banana effects on Parkinson apathy remain open.

Coriander seed blood-pressure trials outside Parkinson disease found no clear between-arm difference versus placebo and measured no postural orthostasis, while leaf studies are limited to rat diuresis and in vitro ACE assays and a Parkinson diet listed coriander without plant part or standing symptoms; dried cilantro effects on Parkinson orthostatic lightheadedness remain open.

Raw romaine lettuce has no controlled Parkinson resting-tremor study: a healthy-adult salad crossover (PMID:34261489) measured vascular outcomes without tremor, a red-lettuce fly assay measured climbing, and historical/toxicology wild-lettuce reports involve unrelated Lactuca virosa species or injections.

Cooked shiitake mushroom has no controlled resting-tremor study: mouse Parkinson-model experiments (PMID:39264814, PMID:42015685) tested purified lentinan or engineered lentinan carriers on pole/general motor tests without reporting rest tremor or cooked whole mushroom exposure.

Ground paprika has no controlled Parkinson resting-tremor study: acute rodent toxicity studies of isolated oral capsaicin (PMID:8887888) and concentrated dermal capsaicinoid gel (PMID:41674738) noted nonspecific toxic tremor without testing culinary sweet paprika or clinical rest tremor.

Dried dill weed has no controlled resting-tremor study: an oral mixed-extract stroke study measured aggregate NIHSS, a rodent alcohol-withdrawal assay of concentrated sowa extract tested coordination, and seed assays were cellular only.

Ground caraway has no controlled Parkinson resting-tremor study: the sole relevant toxicology record (ECHA 2012) noted occasional nonspecific body tremor in two rats after acute isolated carvone dosing without culinary exposure or rest-tremor grading.

Refined corn oil has no isolated Parkinson resting-tremor comparison: Parkinson cannabidiol trials (PMID:25237116, PMID:18801821, PMID:31909680) used corn oil as a shared carrier across arms and an active-lipid trial (DOI:10.1016/j.baga.2014.03.004) lacked a no-oil control or isolated tremor contrast.

Cooked curry leaf (Murraya koenigii) has no clinical Parkinson resting-tremor trial: oral methanol and ethanol leaf extracts reversed reserpine- and haloperidol-induced rat orofacial dyskinesia (VCMs, tongue protrusions, catalepsy; PMID:24250488, PMID:22136413) and improved paraquat/rotenone coordination without isolating Parkinsonian limb rest tremor or cooked culinary leaf.

Cooked wheat berries have no isolated Parkinson resting-tremor comparison: a 57-person Parkinson gluten-free diet trial (NCT05238545) gave an inconclusive composite motor result without isolating whole wheat berries or rest tremor, and celiac withdrawal case reports mix diagnoses and medication changes.

Dried rosemary (Rosmarinus officinalis) has no controlled clinical or preclinical resting-tremor comparison: a Parkinson vegetarian diet pilot (PMID:32041265) listed rosemary in a shared menu with aggregate UPDRS-III only, and isolated carnosic/rosmarinic acid rodent studies targeted levodopa dyskinesia (PMID:34434108) or general MPTP locomotion rather than rest tremor.

Cold-pressed flaxseed oil has no isolated resting-tremor effect: in early Parkinson disease (PMID:34127758, n=38), plasma alpha-linolenic acid showed a near-zero correlation with examiner-rated rest tremor (rho=0.059, p=0.728), and two flaxseed omega-3 plus vitamin E RCTs (PMID:28342967, DOI:10.1016/j.clineuro.2018.12.006) co-administered vitamin E without reporting an isolated rest-tremor item.

Raw apple has no isolated clinical or whole-fruit Parkinson resting-tremor study: Parkinson motor-task cohorts used apples only as chewing/eating test props and mixed menus reported composite UPDRS only; isolated quercetin attenuated 6-OHDA rat muscle tremor (PMID:26217978) and harmaline mouse essential tremor (PMID:41354816, n=32, p<0.0001), but quercetin is ubiquitous across many foods and neither study tested an apple preparation.

Ground cardamom (Elettaria cardamomum) has no controlled resting-tremor comparison: a Parkinson diet menu (PMID:32041265) reported only aggregate UPDRS-III, and isolated cardamonin rodent/cellular studies (PMID:42975774, PMID:41803928) measured open-field, pole-climbing, catalepsy, and microglial NF-kB rather than rest tremor or ground spice.

Cold-pressed hazelnut oil has no clinical or preclinical resting-tremor comparison: analytical studies measure filbertone in cold-pressed oils (Bendini 2014), whole hazelnuts appear only in a mixed Parkinson menu (PMID:32041265), and isolated filbertone mouse experiments (PMID:36958418, PMID:39636503) measured rotarod, treadmill, and neurotrophic markers without rest tremor.

Ground nutmeg has no culinary-dose Parkinson resting-tremor trial: poison-center series and accidental overdose reports (PMID:39559662, PMID:24452991, PMID:24998027, PMID:26219944, DOI:10.3166/afmu-2022-0380) document acute toxicosis with mixed upper-limb or intention tremor alongside delirium or hyponatremia rather than culinary intake or Parkinson rest tremor, while a haloperidol mouse extract study (Palupi 2024) tested rotarod/cylinder only.

One double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial in 90 older adults with age-associated memory impairment (PMID29314866) reports improved Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire ease of getting to sleep with 900 mg/day dried aqueous spearmint extract versus placebo (p=.0046, d=0.805; overall p=.0170), while sleep quality (p=.4267) and ease of awakening (p=.9016) were null. A larger 90-day trial of the same proprietary extract in 142 healthy active young adults (PMID30802720) found inconclusive LSEQ and PSQI comparisons, a spearmint-plus-green-tea blend trial (PMID33809544) had null primary outcomes alongside an exploratory ISI gain (p=.044) without isolated attribution, and a rat pentobarbital-sleep study (PMID30158996) prolonged induced sleep duration. Sponsor funding, concentrated extract capsules rather than culinary dried spearmint leaves, non-Parkinson cohorts, and the competing null trial in younger adults keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

One randomized intention-to-treat trial in 68 adults with migraine (PMID41478596, IRCT20230616058497N1) reports greater eight-week Insomnia Severity Index reduction with oral flaxseed powder versus roasted wheat powder (-4.6 vs -1.6, p=.029) alongside headache-severity improvement. An uncontrolled 46-student pilot of roasted whole flaxseed (DOI10.5455/jrtm.2022/97416) found shorter polysomnography sleep latency (p<.001), inconclusive global PSQI (p=.635), and a text-versus-table Epworth Sleepiness Scale discrepancy without a comparison arm. Powdered whole seed rather than cold-pressed flaxseed oil and a migraine rather than Parkinson cohort keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

One randomized trial in 90 adults with knee osteoarthritis (PMID42866378, PMC13657636) reports lower immediate post-three-week WOMAC pain with topical 3% tarragon oil extract in sweet almond oil versus vehicle and routine care (10.13 vs 13.73 and 13.43, p=.001), while one- and three-week post-stop contrasts were inconclusive (p=.376 and .858), scent prevented blinding, and the 2021 registry disagrees on chronology, randomization, schedule and blinding. Supporting oral animal evidence shows aqueous dried tarragon aerial-part extract lowered formalin-evoked pain in fructose-fed rats (PMID26170888, p<.001), whereas ethanolic extract PMI-5011 in high-fat-diet mice normalized evoked neuropathy thresholds rather than spontaneous pain (PMID20396384), and a completed dental-gel registry (IRCT20241115063712N1) has no public results. Topical and dried-extract exposures, non-Parkinson cohorts, transient effect, and registration discrepancies keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

One randomized controlled trial in 54 adults with heterogeneous pain (DOI10.15806/j.issn.2311-8571.2015.0032) reports lower immediate post-inhalation 0-10 pain after 15 minutes of Piper nigrum essential oil versus sesame oil (median 3 vs 6, Mann-Whitney U=117.5, p<.001; baseline 6 vs 7, p=.930) without verifying scent masking, supported by oral standardized black-pepper seed extract in diabetic-rat tail-flick testing (PMID35733641) and high-dose oral isolated piperine in rat paw/arthritis models (PMID19327174). Conversely, the closest oral culinary comparisonâ€”a 29-adult chronic-pain crossover adding 300 mg/day ground black pepper to background ground turmeric for one-week periods (PMID41599836)â€”gave an inconclusive pepper-addition contrast (p=.157, treatment-by-period p=.5508), and no clinical study shows black pepper worsening pain. Inhalation route, unverified scent blinding, the inconclusive ground-pepper add-on crossover, and non-Parkinson cohorts limit the easing lean contradicting the worsening hypothesis to minimal_signal.

Two Parkinson-relevant rodent experiments show longer measured stride length after oral pumpkin-seed preparations or a documented constituent: haloperidol-exposed rats given ascending methanolic Cucurbita pepo seed extract arms had figure-derived mean stride lengths of 6.4, 7.3 and 8.0 cm versus 5.7 cm in disease controls (PMID33759084, Figure 4; group counts and comparator footnotes unverified), and haloperidol-exposed mice (n=6/group) given higher oral isolated p-coumaric acid had longer day-21 stride than untreated controls (DOI10.1177/0976500X221150837, p<.05 and p<.01). Roasting-chemistry analysis confirms measurable p-coumaric acid (0.5-0.6 ug/g) and ferulic acid (0.9-1.8 ug/g) in 130-150 C roasted pressed pumpkin seed oil (DOI10.1002/ejlt.201700110) without establishing food-to-extract dose equivalence. Animal-only gait evidence, extract-versus-oil exposure gaps, and absence of human Parkinson testing keep the easing signal contradicting the worsening hypothesis at minimal_signal.

One randomized placebo-controlled 30-day trial in 86 university students (NCT05999071, DOI10.1108/nfs-08-2023-0193) reports lower anxiety with dried powdered Coriandrum sativum seed capsules versus starch placebo (p=.04), although retrospective registration after completion, shifting anxiety from secondary to primary, and absent posted arm-level data limit reliability. Supporting animal evidence shows aqueous and oil fractions of hydroethanolic cilantro leaf extract produced anxiolytic signals in mouse elevated plus maze and light-dark box tests without rotarod deficit (DOI10.18203/2319-2003.ijbcp20202936), whereas an earlier dried-cilantro-leaf mouse study (PMID26109787) is unusable for direction due to internal abstract-versus-methods route and extraction conflicts. Seed-versus-leaf plant-part differences, non-Parkinson population, and reporting gaps keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

One patent-reported human randomized crossover in 14 healthy men (WO2019230626A1) reports -0.24 fewer nighttime urinations per night versus starch after 28 days of commercial red-perilla (Perilla frutescens) water extract (p<.05) from a low 0.24 baseline, while daytime frequency and daily urine volume contrasts were inconclusive and table-versus-prose daytime standard errors conflict. Independently, oral perilla extract prolonged micturition inter-void intervals by 27% versus controls in female spontaneously hypertensive rats without altering maximum bladder pressure (PMID29268303). Extract-versus-fresh-shiso exposure, small non-Parkinson healthy-male patent cohort, void-frequency rather than urgency-episode measurement, and daytime null contrasts keep the easing signal contradicting the worsening hypothesis at minimal_signal.

One controlled 6-OHDA medial-forebrain-bundle rat Parkinson model experiment (PMID25050252, PMC4075680; 38 Wistar rats across five groups of 7-8) reports significantly lower three-stage cumulative muscle stiffness/rigidity scores after 28 days of oral hydroalcoholic red grape (Vitis vinifera) seed extract 100 mg/kg/day versus untreated lesioned and vehicle-lesioned controls (Kruskal-Wallis and median test, p<.01, Figure 2B), while remaining above intact/sham controls (p<.05). A separate 6-OHDA rat red-grape-juice study measured apomorphine turning without a verified juice-versus-lesion contrast (PMC4075659), and a human Parkinson grape-juice plus aquatic-exercise trial recorded motor scores at baseline only (PMID32798568). Seed-extract rather than whole frozen-grape exposure (with seedless grape variability) and animal-only rigidity data keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

Two randomized human controlled trials report reduced acute procedural pain with topical clove preparations: a split-mouth placebo-controlled trial in 73 adults found glycerin gel prepared with ground clove lowered dental needle-insertion pain versus placebo (PMID16530911, p=.005), and a double-blind crossover in 34 hemodialysis patients found topical eugenol nanoemulsion lowered cannulation puncture pain versus no intervention and placebo gel (PMID32951708, p=.001; placebo mean omitted from public abstract). Competing studies show inconclusive three-arm postoperative headache contrasts for inhaled clove aromatherapy (PMID40012817, p=.20 at 8 h and p=.31 at 24 h), an unquantified null mouse hot-water report for ground clove powder (CCRAS 1997-1998), and assay-dependent rat essential-oil nanogel formalin versus hot-plate results (PMC9123718). Topical procedural versus oral chronic Parkinson pain and competing null trials keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

One controlled mouse experiment (Bian 2019; 10 mice per group across five arms) reports lower 20-minute acetic-acid-evoked writhing counts after oral volatile fractions from dry-fried (toasted) and raw huajiao versus vehicle (18.40 and 21.10 dry-fried, 19.50 and 27.20 raw vs 49.60 vehicle), although full-text methods, fried-versus-raw comparison, and botanical species voucher remain unverified. Local application of isolated hydroxy-alpha-sanshool reduced inflammatory mechanical hypersensitivity without altering heat hypersensitivity in mice (PMID23652591), an uncontrolled nine-woman xerostomia series of mixed Zanthoxylum oil capsules noted oral-discomfort gains without placebo (PMC6392883), and a 40-woman placebo-controlled IBS trial of multi-herb daikenchuto was null for abdominal and rectal pain without isolating Sichuan pepper (PMID26486374). Volatile-fraction rather than whole toasted spice, unverified full-text details, multi-herb clinical nullity, and absence of Parkinson pain data keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

One double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial in 82 healthy adults aged 30-55 (Kennedy 2019, PMID31835620, PMC6950039, NCT03673930) reports lower day-56 cognitive-task mental fatigue with 80 mg/day standardized Zanthoxylum armatum extract in MCT oil versus sunflower-oil placebo (p=.006), although pretreatment mental fatigue was already higher in the extract arm and primary registered endpoint was chronic secondary memory. Two healthy-gamer extract crossover registrations with fatigue outcomes (NCT07047105, NCT07752329) have no posted results. Standardized extract versus culinary ground Sichuan pepper, non-Parkinson healthy sample, and baseline imbalance keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

One randomized four-arm trial in 104 adults with functional dyspepsia (85 analyzed; Saravani 2025, PMID40365186, PMC12068504) reports greater week-8 constipation subscore improvement for aqueous Rhus coriaria (sumac) extract alone (n=24) and combined with eating-habit changes (n=25) versus omeprazole (n=25) in adjusted model 6 (p=.002 and p<.001) with zero adverse events, although unadjusted contrasts were unstated and effect magnitudes/confidence intervals were omitted from Table 6. Conversely, a preclinical mouse castor-oil diarrhea and rabbit jejunum study found crude sumac extract slowed induced diarrhea and relaxed intestinal contractions (DOI10.3329/bjp.v9i4.20879). Active omeprazole comparator, aqueous extract versus ground sumac, non-Parkinson dyspepsia cohort, and unreported effect sizes keep the easing lean contradicting the worsening hypothesis at minimal_signal.

One published human clinical case of focal eyelid dystonia (blepharospasm; Leon-Sarmiento 2005, PMID16258648) reports a decline in rated dystonia severity from 4 at baseline to 1 at six months following transdermal capsaicin patch treatment, alongside an inconclusive blink-rate check in five healthy volunteers (17 +- 3 vs 15 +- 5).
