Uncontrolled single-patient design, topical isolated capsaicin patch rather than oral ground cayenne pepper, and focal non-Parkinson blepharospasm rather than Parkinson dystonia keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

One double-blind randomized placebo-controlled crossover in healthy volunteers (Tanaka 2008; 18 randomized, 17 analyzed) reports smaller visual-analogue fatigue increases after 29 days of oral chicken-breast extract drink (400 mg/day imidazole dipeptides) versus placebo following four hours of cycling (+18.1 +- 15.8 vs +26.3 +- 18.1 mm, p<.05) and four hours of recovery (+9.8 +- 17.3 vs +20.1 +- 20.7 mm, p<.01), whereas two-hour, next-day, and end-of-exercise recovery contrasts were null; food chemistry confirms anserine and carnosine retention in heated chicken breast (DOI10.3136/nskkk.66.210). Conversely, a 30-adult randomized crossover of reconstituted whole-chicken soup found inconclusive routine POMS fatigue changes (-0.5 vs +0.1, p=.61; DOI10.1248/jhs.55.56), a sprint extract trial had inconclusive power outcomes (PMID16531904), and a culinary patent tasting report (KR20050019309A) lacks controlled symptom measurement. Concentrated dipeptide drink versus poached chicken, healthy exercise-induced fatigue rather than Parkinson fatigue, small sample, and competing null chicken-soup crossover keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

Multiple independent oral curcuminoid experiments in Parkinson-model rodents show improved bradykinesia and locomotor speed proxies versus lesioned controls: oral curcumin shortened pole-descent latency and raised open-field mean speed in MPTP mice (PMID37388445, p<.01 each), oral intragastric curcumin 160 mg/kg/day for two weeks improved open-field average speed, distance and rotarod latency in 6-OHDA rats (PMID37484231, PMC10360947, n=6/group; 40/80 mg/kg limited), middle-dose oral curcumin improved pole descent in MPTP mice (PMID36034698), oral curcumin improved pole descent and mobility time in rats (PMID40208367), oral demethoxycurcumin attenuated rotenone rat motor deficits (PMID29576695, PMC5858249), and curcumin nanoparticles enhanced MPTP mouse movement time and activity (PMID41878684, PMC13006185). In human Parkinson studies, nanomicelle curcumin showed a composite Part III time-by-treatment p=.04 without a separate bradykinesia item (PMID35636380), and a nonrandomized phospholipid-curcuminoid cohort noted slower OFF composite progression (+5 vs +11, PMID35556131). Conversely, a non-Parkinson curcumin walking trial gave numerically smaller 400-m gait-speed gain than placebo (+.014 vs +.103 m/s, NCT03085680) and young non-Parkinson mice fed isolated curcumin showed poorer skilled pellet reaching with null open-field movement (PMID24723215). Isolated curcuminoid extracts rather than culinary ground turmeric, rodent-only bradykinesia items, and competing non-PD gait/reaching data keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

Two independent randomized placebo-controlled human trials of coated proprietary Cucumis melo cantaloupe juice concentrate (Extramel 10 mg/day) report reduced subjective fatigue in stressed or healthy adults: a four-week trial in 70 adults reported 26% greater day-28 FARD weariness improvement versus placebo (Milesi 2009, PMID19754931, PMC2757026), and an 84-day trial in 61 healthy adults reported lower day-84 Prevost physical fatigue versus placebo (84.4 vs 93.2, p<.02; day-28 null; Carillon 2014, PMID24949549, PMC4073155, NCT01767922). Conversely, three competing randomized trials of melon SOD/gliadin or dried melon concentrate were null on fatigue (Houghton 2010 PMID21044831 n=38; SODB 2020 PMID32053942 p=.068; GliSODin 2022 PMID35628874 n=46 p=.15). Proprietary palm-oil-coated concentrate versus raw cantaloupe, non-Parkinson cohorts, and three competing null trials keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

One double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial in 82 healthy adults aged 30-55 (Kennedy 2019, PMID31835620, PMC6950039, NCT03673930) reports faster acute Speed of Attention (p=.039) and fewer rapid visual information processing false alarms (p=.025) with 80 mg/day standardized Zanthoxylum armatum extract in MCT oil versus sunflower-oil placebo, while baseline false alarms were higher in the extract arm, name-to-face memory accuracy moved unfavorably (p=.040), and chronic secondary memory was the registered primary endpoint. Two healthy-gamer extract crossover registrations targeting attention speed and accuracy (NCT07047105, NCT07752329) have no posted results. Standardized extract versus culinary toasted Sichuan pepper, healthy non-Parkinson sample, mixed cognitive domain signs, and baseline imbalance keep the easing lean contradicting the worsening hypothesis at minimal_signal.
